overview: The Marathon County Infrastructure Committee held a brief meeting focused primarily on public comment from two Town of Texas residents about dangerous conditions on County Road W, followed by approval of the 2026 Marathon County Culvert Bridge Aid resolution. The committee voted to forward the bridge aid resolution to the county board, covering approximately $64,000 in culvert and bridge projects completed by county crews for local municipalities.

discussions.item: Public Comment - County Road W Safety Concerns
discussions.body: Two Town of Texas residents, Tracy Delaney (236617 County Road W) and Donald Hillbrand (236493 County Road W), spoke about dangerous conditions on County Road W. Delaney requested no-engine-braking signs due to noise from increased truck traffic from Hos, and asked the committee to add guardrails on the east side of County Road W north of Marshall Hill Road when road improvements are planned, noting her house is only 30 feet from the road. Hillbrand echoed concerns about out-of-control speeds, outdated and unsafe guardrails, vehicles crossing into driveways and nearly striking his house, and a semi that refused to yield to an ambulance — for which Sheriff Chad Bilip fined the driver and firm $500 each. Hillbrand noted that a consulting firm had agreed guardrails were needed.

Kevin [last name not stated] presented the 2026 Culvert Bridge Aid program, describing it as a fairly typical year with approximately $64,000 in projects, with county crews completing five projects for municipalities. A larger box culvert project for the Town of McMillan was excluded from this resolution because it received 90% state funding through the Local Small Structure Improvement Program (LSSIP) for 6-to-20-foot structures, though crews still plan to complete it in October. The committee voted unanimously to forward Resolution 5726 to the county board; the motion was made by Griner and seconded by [inaudible, referred to as 'AC'].

discussions.item: Announcements - North Central Region Fall Legislative Meeting
discussions.body: Kevin announced that the North Central Region fall legislative meeting is scheduled for October 23rd in Stevens Point, featuring a breakfast at 8:30 a.m. with presentations from commissioners and transportation officials, and with all legislators invited. He noted the registration deadline is October 2nd and asked interested committee members to contact him.

publicComment: Two speakers offered public comment. Tracy Delaney of 236617 County Road W in the Town of Texas requested no-engine-braking signs due to noise from increased truck traffic and asked that guardrails be added to the east side of County Road W north of Marshall Hill Road during planned road improvements. Donald Hillbrand of 236493 County Road W in the Town of Texas described dangerous speeding, vehicles entering his property, a trailer nearly striking his house, and a semi blocking an ambulance — citing video evidence shared with Sheriff Chad Bilip. Both residents called for updated guardrails and traffic safety improvements.
